stem.text: Let \( f(x) = 3 \sin\left(2x\right) \). Find the first 4 nonzero terms and the general term of the Maclaurin series for f.

worked_solution.text: Start from the Maclaurin series for \( \sin x \) and replace x by \( 2x \), raising the whole of \( 2x \) to each power.
Multiply every term by \( 3 \); the first 4 nonzero terms are \( 6 x - 4 x^{3} + \frac{4}{5} x^{5} - \frac{8}{105} x^{7} \).
The general term is \( \frac{3 \cdot (-1)^{n} 2^{2n+1} x^{2n+1}}{(2n+1)!} \); putting n = 0, 1, 2 reproduces the terms above.

options.label: \( 6 x + 4 x^{3} + \frac{4}{5} x^{5} + \frac{8}{105} x^{7} + \cdots + \frac{3 \cdot 2^{2n+1} x^{2n+1}}{(2n+1)!} + \cdots \)
options.derivation: the series for sin x recalled without its alternating signs

options.label: \( 6 x - x^{3} + \frac{1}{20} x^{5} - \frac{1}{840} x^{7} + \cdots + \frac{3 \cdot (-1)^{n} 2 x^{2n+1}}{(2n+1)!} + \cdots \)
options.derivation: x replaced by 2x but 2 not raised to the power of each term

options.label: \( 6 x - 4 x^{3} + \frac{4}{5} x^{5} - \frac{8}{105} x^{7} + \cdots + \frac{3 \cdot (-1)^{n+1} 2^{2n+3} x^{2n+3}}{(2n+3)!} + \cdots \)
options.derivation: the general term written with n + 1 where n belongs, so at n = 0 it gives the second term rather than the first
